instructions.task: Tag the final persuader message (after 'Persuader message to tag:') with the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses. The chat is between a persuader and a persuadee; the persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate part of their task payment to Save the Children. Use the earlier dialogue only as context for what the message responds to.
rules: Tag what the message itself does; if it does several things, pick its main act.
Facts about the charity are credibility even when answering a question; bare yes/no answers are answer-to-question.
Statistics about children's suffering are suffering (emotion), not donation-impact.

criteria.greeting: Opening pleasantry or introduction: hello, hi, how are you, and replies to how-are-you such as I am doing well / doing ok here / fine, and you?, nice to meet you.
criteria.closing: Goodbye or closing remark without thanks: have a great day/night, take care, bye, good luck.
criteria.thank: Expresses gratitude to the persuadee, for themself or on behalf of the children or charity: thank you, thanks for your time, thanks for donating, the children will appreciate it, we appreciate your help (even if combined with a goodbye).
criteria.you-are-welcome: Replies to the persuadee's thanks: you're welcome, no problem.
criteria.praise-user: Explicitly compliments the persuadee as a person (a bare 'that's great' is not praise): you are kind/generous/a good person, people like you make the world better, that's so generous of you.
criteria.acknowledgement: Brief agreement or positive reaction to what the persuadee just said, adding no new content: ok, I see, I understand, I agree, me too, that's true, that's great, good, right, indeed, I know.
criteria.answer-to-question: A yes/no or short answer to a question the persuadee asked, possibly with a brief opinion (e.g. 'Yes, they are.', 'Yes, I think they are great.', 'Absolutely.' in reply to a question), that gives no concrete fact about the charity.
criteria.confirm-donation: Confirms, restates or reacts to a donation amount the persuadee has already agreed to: 'so you'll donate $1, right?', 'that's great!' right after they state their amount.
criteria.comment-partner: A comment on the persuadee, their situation or opinion that is not a compliment and not a question, including disagreeing with them ('I disagree but see your point').
criteria.task-management: Talk about running this chat/HIT itself: how many turns are needed, offering to provide more information, clarifying a typo, meta remarks about the conversation.
criteria.persuader-self-disclosure: The persuader mentions their own job, volunteering or charity work (e.g. 'I work with abused children', 'I volunteer at a food bank', 'I have worked with charities before') without saying they donate money to this cause.
criteria.misc-other: A persuader remark that fits none of the other options.
criteria.off-task: Chitchat unrelated to donation, charity or the children: weather, work, where they live, celebrities, history unrelated to the cause.
criteria.charity-identity: Facts about Save the Children itself: what it is, what it does, its programs and where it works, its history and founder, even when answering the persuadee's question.
criteria.charity-reputation: Unprompted claims about the charity's trustworthiness or reputation: it is trustworthy, well known, top rated; how its funds are spent (e.g. 86% goes to programs); pointing to its website or URL to learn more.
criteria.suffering: Describes children's suffering or evokes emotion: sadness, sympathy, guilt, fear, hope; statistics about children dying, hungry, killed or displaced; 'imagine your child...'; the persuader's own feelings about the children's plight; a brief mention of someone they know who suffered or lost a child.
criteria.donation-impact: Reasoning about why to help or the effect of donating: every child deserves a chance and we can change a life, your donation will make a difference, money goes to help children, every little bit helps, any amount helps, small amounts add up, if everyone gave a little.
criteria.small-ask: Asks for, or stresses how little is needed, a small or minimal amount to lower the barrier (not when the message mainly expresses sadness or guilt, which is suffering): it only takes pocket change, 'could you afford maybe fifteen cents?', 'even $0.50 would help, could you give that?', 'just 10 cents'.
criteria.proposition: Asks, invites or urges the persuadee to donate, including 'are you interested in donating?', 'would you consider donating to them?', 'we should donate', or suggesting a specific amount that is not small.
criteria.ask-amount: Asks how much the persuadee will or would like to donate, without suggesting a figure.
criteria.donation-procedure: Explains how the donation works or where the donated money goes: it is deducted from the task payment, any amount from $0 to the full payment, the research team collects and sends it to Save the Children, matching offers.
criteria.self-modeling: The persuader says they themself donate money or will donate (to set an example): I will donate too, I'll match your amount, I give to this cause yearly.
criteria.personal-story: The persuader narrates a story (several events) about a specific person or their own past experience related to the cause: a child who was helped, their own time working abroad. Also the persuader's own past experience or hesitation with donating ('I thought about donating before but never got around to it'). A one-line mention of someone suffering is suffering, not a story.
criteria.source-inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee knows about Save the Children: have you heard of them? are you familiar with the organization? do you know what they do?
criteria.task-inquiry: Asks the persuadee's views or experience about charity, donating or the cause (not an invitation to donate now): do you donate to charities? have you donated before? do you care about children's rights? what do you think?
criteria.personal-inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life, habits or spending beyond the greeting: do you have kids? where are you from? how is your day going? what do you do? how much do you spend on candy?
